AMD delivers differentiated solutions including semi-custom SoCs, Adaptive SoCs, and APUs at the chip level, and client computing devices, embedded platforms, and servers at the platform level, with specific product lines for data center, adaptive/embedded, client, and gaming markets.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel launched Intel Xeon 6 processors for data centers using Intel 3 process and Efficient cores, designed to address diverse workload deployments. The 5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors, based on Intel 7, continued to ramp throughout 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel explicitly detail the launch and strategic importance of their 5th generation server processor families in the data center segment during 2024, marking a parallel focus on next-generation CPU product roadmaps. However, they differ in specific product nomenclature and architectural focus: AMD highlights the '5th Gen AMD EPYC' family for general data center workloads, while Intel details the '5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable' processors alongside the newer 'Xeon 6' processors leveraging Efficient cores (E-cores) on the Intel 3 process.

sentences.text: We announced our 5th Gen AMD EPYC™ family of server processors, providing leadership performance and capabilities for a wide range of data center workloads.

▪Data center CPUs. We launched our Intel® Xeon® 6 processors for the data center, utilizing the Intel 3 process, including our first Intel Xeon processor using Efficient cores (E-cores). The Intel Xeon 6 family is designed to address the growing diversity in workloads and deployments in the data center environments. Our 5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors, based on Intel 7, were launched in 2023, and continued to ramp throughout 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: CNBU data center sales were driven by server demand in cloud and enterprise markets, with growth fueled by the shift of infrastructure and workloads to the cloud and the memory-intensive nature of AI data-centric workloads.
comparisons.comparison: While AMD identifies strong demand from hyperscaler customers as a primary driver for its Data Center segment growth, Micron attributes data center market performance to broader cloud and enterprise server demand and the memory-intensive nature of AI workloads. AMD focuses on its own GPU/CPU product deployment success, whereas Micron focuses on the underlying memory infrastructure (HBM/DRAM) requirements driven by the same AI and cloud shifts that fuel AMD's server processor and accelerator sales.

sentences.text: The demand for our data center AI accelerator products was very strong as large hyperscaler customers, OEMs and ODMs deployed our AMD Instinct™ MI300X GPUs.
One of our priorities in 2024 was to accelerate growth in our Data Center segment.
Data center: CNBU sales to the data center end market were driven primarily by server demand across the cloud and enterprise markets and solutions offered to the networking market.

Cloud servers supporting AI and data-centric workloads require significantly increasing quantities of DRAM, including HBM, and NAND as the task of turning data into insight becomes increasingly memory-centric.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Compute & Networking segment comprises Data Center accelerated computing and end-to-end networking platforms (including InfiniBand and Ethernet), NVIDIA DRIVE automated-driving platform, Jetson robotics, AI Enterprise software, and DGX Cloud services.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA structure their primary business strategy around 'Data Center' accelerated computing platforms as a core segment. AMD describes this as its 'Data Center segment' encompassing EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs, while NVIDIA defines its 'Compute & Networking segment' which comprises 'Data Center accelerated computing platforms.' Both disclosures position data center workloads as the central hub for their respective hardware and software ecosystems.

sentences.text: One of our priorities in 2024 was to accelerate growth in our Data Center segment.
The demand for our data center AI accelerator products was very strong as large hyperscaler customers, OEMs and ODMs deployed our AMD Instinct™ MI300X GPUs.

The Compute & Networking segment is comprised of our Data Center accelerated computing platforms and end-to-end networking platforms including Quantum for InfiniBand and Spectrum for Ethernet; our NVIDIA DRIVE automated-driving platform and automotive development agreements; Jetson robotics and other embedded platforms; NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software; and DGX Cloud software and services.
